newsitem.title: USA: CME LUMBER TUMBLES AT CLOSE ON WEAK CASH MARKET.
newsitem.headline: CME LUMBER TUMBLES AT CLOSE ON WEAK CASH MARKET.

text.p: Reports that cash lumber offerings were increasing amid slow sales pushed CME lumber futures through technical support levels to a sharply lower close, traders said.
September fell for a near-limit loss of $9.90 per tbf before ending $9.40 lower at $350.50 per tbf. November finished $4.60 lower at $345.50 and other months ended $2.60 lower to unchanged.
Current high mill asking prices and lack of trade weighed on futures with fund selling adding to pressure as the market cut through moving averages, traders said.
"There's plenty of wood in the pipeline," one trader said.
Cash sources noted that secondaries are now trying to find buyers for their wood and this will likely prompt cash mills to lower asking prices later in the week.
Cargill Investor Services notably sold September into the close. Fimat Futures USA spread long November/short September earlier, pit sources said.
